goals.title: Cast the island's bells
goals.critique: This one is new, and its core is strong: a carved shape, a pour and a broken mould end in a loud, one-of-a-kind answer from the bell's real vibration modes, and the struck bell with the whole island turning to the hill is a real clip. But the pitch is a run-on paragraph, and since no cut can be heard until after a long pour, 'learning what each cut does' may become slow blind guessing unless something lets the player read it sooner. The road stacks several unproven systems (modal FEM on a carved solid, molten flow into sand, cooling defects) on the way to a tuned set nobody has priced, so its cheap first step, three bells that sound clearly different, has to prove it before anything else.

goals.title: Wet the hill and dig
goals.critique: This is round 9's candidate again, the third version of the burrows line, and the only change is a shorter pitch that is still two clauses plus a rule rather than one plain action. What earlier verdicts praised still stands: sand you read at a glance, a sun clock on every wall, sticks that creak before they snap, a dig-out rescue people would send, and the closest fit to the human's direction. But sand that caves in is still familiar from falling-sand and mining games, and after three rounds the damp-stands, dries, trickles and caves film still has not been made, so re-pitching adds nothing until it exists.
